title: Sebastian and the Smile
premise: Theo Nakamura, a hospice nurse who has spent thirty years rationalizing the backwards counting he hears from the dying, returns to his childhood home after his mother's death and finds Sebastian, his imaginary friend, waiting on the porch—unchanged, unaged, and smiling exactly as he did in 1974. Sebastian doesn't want companionship; he wants restitution: something Theo took from the old well behind the house the summer his friend Danny Voss drowned, something that kept Sebastian tethered and Danny's death officially an accident. As the dying patients under Theo's care begin counting backwards toward one date—June 14th—he must excavate the truth of what he saw and buried: that the town's beloved sheriff pushed Danny into the well and made the children swear silence. Returning the taken thing—a photograph proving it—means exposing his own complicity and shattering the loyalty he owed a dead man's memory. In the end, Theo gives the truth to Danny's still-living sister, Sebastian finally ages and fades at the refilled well, and Theo learns that some debts are paid not by forgetting but by remembering out loud.
about_author: Isandro Ashgrove is the pen name of a former hospice volunteer from coastal Oregon who spent four years collecting the last words of the terminally ill before turning to fiction. Their work explores the violence small towns forgive and the children who are made to keep its secrets.

chapters.title: The Porch Light
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. After burying his mother, Theo returns to the family house to pack it up and finds Sebastian on the porch—identical to 1974, smile intact, refusing to be dismissed as grief or exhaustion. That night, a dying patient at the hospice counts backwards and stops at 'fourteen.' The emotional beat is dread disguised as denial: Theo tells himself nothing is wrong while packing boxes around a presence he cannot explain.

chapters.title: What the Well Kept
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Theo and Sebastian. Sebastian leads Theo to the sealed well and demands back what was taken; fragmented memories surface—Danny Voss's bike, Sheriff Hollis's hands, a photograph Theo hid to keep his family safe. Meanwhile hospice patients across town begin counting to the same date. The emotional beat is vertigo: loyalty to the man who protected him warring against the truth he buried at nine years old.

chapters.title: Fourteen Days in June
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Researching Danny's drowning, Theo finds the sheriff's widow still guarding the family name and realizes the whole town's memory was curated. Sebastian grows agitated as June 14th nears—the well is 'refilling,' and whatever wasn't returned will be collected differently. When Theo refuses to hand over the photograph, Sebastian shows him what the well does with secrets. The beat is terror sharpening into resolve: Theo chooses truth over protection.

chapters.title: Refill
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, closing with Danny's sister Ruth. On June 14th, Theo gives Ruth the photograph and his testimony, then opens the well and speaks Danny's name aloud—the first public telling in fifty years. Sebastian, finally aging, thanks him and dissolves as the water rises clean. At the hospice, the counting stops. The beat is grief transmuted into release: justice outside the law, memory restored, and Theo no longer invisible to himself.
